title: Mandarin greetings and tones
examples: How do I say hello in Mandarin?
What are the different tones in Mandarin?
Can you show me how to write pinyin?

explain.say: Today we will learn some basic Mandarin greetings.
Ni hao means hello in Mandarin Chinese.
Mandarin has four main tones you must learn.
We use pinyin to help us read the sounds.
For example, the word ma can mean mother or horse.
In real life, you use tones when greeting friends.

faq.q: Why do tones matter when speaking Mandarin?
faq.a: Tones change the meaning of the word completely. For instance, the same sounds can mean different things based on the tone used.
asks: Do I have to worry about tones?
Will people understand me without tones?

faq.q: What is pinyin and how do I use it?
faq.a: Pinyin is a system that uses the Roman alphabet to write out the Mandarin sounds. It helps learners read the pronunciation before speaking.
asks: What is the alphabet for Mandarin?
How do I read the characters?

faq.q: Are there only four tones to learn?
faq.a: Yes, there are four main tones, plus a neutral tone. Each tone has a distinct pitch pattern you must practice.
asks: Can I learn the tones easily?

faq.q: What is the difference between a tone and a pitch?
faq.a: Pitch is how high or low your voice sounds. A tone is a specific pattern of that pitch over a syllable.
asks: Is tone the same as pitch?

faq.q: How do I practice the tones correctly?
faq.a: The best way is to listen to native speakers often. Try repeating after them many times to get the rhythm right.
asks: What is the best way to practice?

facts: Mandarin Chinese is spoken by hundreds of millions of people.
Pinyin uses the Latin alphabet to represent Mandarin sounds.
The four main tones are high-level, rising, dipping, and falling.
Ni hao is the common way to say hello.

quiz.say: If a word has a rising tone, what does the pitch do?
quiz.why: Tone 2 has a pitch that rises, like when you ask a question.

wrong.0: Tone 4 is always falling, so it does not rise.
wrong.2: Tone 1 is high and flat, so it does not rise.
wrong.3: Tone 3 dips down before rising, it is not just rising.

quiz.say: What does the pinyin 'ni hao' mean?
quiz.why: Ni hao is the standard way to say hello in Mandarin.

wrong.1: This is a different phrase for saying farewell.
wrong.2: Thank you has a completely different set of sounds.
wrong.3: This is a question, not a simple greeting.

quiz.say: If I say the same sound with a falling tone, what happens?

options.show: I must use a different word
options.say: I must use a different word

quiz.why: Because tones change the meaning, the word means something different.

wrong.0: While gestures help, the tone is part of the spoken word.
wrong.2: The tone itself is the important part, not just the sound.
wrong.3: You can use the same sound with a different tone.
